name: Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel and chunk the potatoes and get them going in salted water. Slice the onions thin and mince the garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet and brown the sausages slowly on all sides. Low and slow keeps the casings from splitting.
Move the sausages to a plate and start the gravy in the same pan, melting most of the butter and cooking the sliced onions until they go deep golden and sweet.
Add the garlic, then sprinkle in the flour and stir for a minute before streaming in the chicken broth while whisking.
Add the soy sauce and simmer the gravy until it thickens and coats a spoon, then season with salt and black pepper.
Drain the potatoes, mash them with the remaining butter, salt and pepper, and keep them loose enough to portion easily.
Warm the peas through, slice the sausages into thick coins, and combine everything with the gravy in your big pot.
head_steps: Boil the peeled and chunked potatoes in salted water.
Brown the sausages slowly in vegetable oil, then set them aside.
Cook the sliced onions in butter until deep golden, add the garlic, then stir in the flour.
Stream in the chicken broth and soy sauce and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Mash the potatoes with butter, warm the peas, slice the sausages, and combine with the gravy.

name: Lean BBQ Chicken and Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Rice (Member's Mark): 3.5 cups dry jasmine (700 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 5 cups, drained (840 g)
BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) (Sweet Baby Ray's): about 7/8 cup (224 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
Olive Oil: ~2 tbsp to cook chicken (90 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste / rub (4 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Cube the chicken breast and cook in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside.
Turn the heat to low, pour in the BBQ sauce, and toss until every piece is coated.
Drain the corn and warm it through.
Combine the rice, BBQ chicken, and corn in your big pot and stir. Fold in the shredded cheddar.
head_steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Cube and cook the chicken breast in a large skillet until it reaches 165F.
Lower the heat, add the BBQ sauce, and toss to coat.
Drain and warm the corn.
Combine rice, BBQ chicken, and corn in a large pot and fold in the cheddar.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 equal containers.

name: High-Protein Beef Burrito Bowls
ingredients: 93/7 Ground Beef (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Rice (Member's Mark): 3.5 cups dry jasmine (700 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4 cans (910 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 5 cups (840 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (8 oz bag) (196 g)
Tomato Paste (Great Value): 1 tbsp (per 4 servings) (55 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks. At 93/7 there is little to drain.
Add the taco seasoning and a splash of water. Stir until the beef is coated and glossy.
Drain and rinse the black beans and corn, then warm them through.
Combine the rice, beef, beans, and corn in your big pot and stir. Fold in the shredded mozzarella so it melts into the warm mix.
head_steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the taco seasoning with a splash of water until the beef is coated.
Drain and rinse the beans and corn, then warm them through.
Combine rice, beef, beans, and corn in a large pot and fold in the mozzarella.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 equal containers.

name: Beef Chili Rice Bowls
ingredients: 93/7 Ground Beef (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Rice (Member's Mark): 3.5 cups dry jasmine (700 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4 cans, drained (910 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 1/2 cups, drained (420 g)
Beef Broth (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups (420 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Brown the ground beef in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up. Drain any excess.
Stir in the tomato paste and taco seasoning and cook for a minute to bloom the flavor.
Add the drained beans, corn, and beef broth. Simmer 10 to 15 minutes until it thickens into a chili.
Serve each bowl over rice and top with the shredded cheddar.
head_steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Brown the ground beef in a large pot and drain any excess.
Stir in tomato paste and taco seasoning and cook 1 minute.
Add beans, corn, and beef broth and simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Serve over rice and top with cheddar.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.

name: Beef Chow Mein Noodles
ingredients: Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 49.5 oz dry (1400 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 6.75 oz (189 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the lo mein noodles 1 minute short of package directions, drain, rinse briefly with cool water, and toss with a splash of the oil so they do not clump.
Whisk the sauce: soy sauce, oyster sauce, chicken broth, sugar, and flour. Set it by the stove.
Heat a little oil in your largest skillet or wok over high heat. Scramble the beaten eggs into ribbons, then set them aside.
Add more oil and brown the ground beef with the garlic, breaking it up, until no pink remains; ground beef should hit 160F. Season with salt and pepper.
Pile in the shredded cabbage and carrots and stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes until they wilt but keep a little crunch.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens, then add the noodles, eggs, and green onions and toss until everything is glossy and coated.
head_steps: Boil the noodles 1 minute short of package time, drain, and toss with a little oil.
Whisk soy sauce, oyster sauce, broth, sugar, and flour into a sauce.
Scramble the eggs into ribbons and set aside.
Brown the ground beef with garlic to 160F, then stir-fry the cabbage and carrots until just wilted.
Thicken the sauce in the pan, toss in noodles, eggs, and green onions, and portion into 14 containers.

name: Cuban Beef Picadillo Rice Bowls
ingredients: Salt (Morton): 1/8 to 1/2 tsp fine salt (6 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion, green pepper, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce, cumin, oregano, olives, capers, golden raisins, and the bay leaf.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes so the flavors come together, then fish out the bay leaf and season with the salt and black pepper.
Cook the rice while the picadillo simmers.
Spoon the beef over rice and serve.
head_steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion, green pepper, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce, cumin, oregano, olives, capers, golden raisins, and the bay leaf.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes, then remove the bay leaf and season with salt and pepper.
Cook the rice while the picadillo simmers.
Spoon the beef over rice and portion into 14 containers.

name: Bistek Tagalog (Filipino Beef and Onions over Rice)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the beef thin against the grain. Toss it with the lemon juice, soy sauce, minced garlic, and black pepper, then let it sit at least 30 minutes while you prep everything else.
Slice the onions into rings. Fry them in a little of the oil over medium heat until soft and just starting to brown, then pull them out and set them aside.
Lift the beef out of the marinade and save every drop of that liquid. Sear the beef in batches over high heat so it browns instead of steaming.
Return all the beef to the pot, pour in the reserved marinade and a splash of water, and bring it to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, until the beef is tender and the sauce has thickened into a glaze.
Cook the rice separately while the beef simmers.
Stir the fried onions back in for the last 2 minutes, taste, and add salt only if the soy sauce did not carry it far enough.
head_steps: Slice the beef thin and marinate it in lemon juice, soy sauce, garlic, and pepper.
Fry the onion rings in oil until soft, then set them aside.
Sear the drained beef in batches over high heat.
Add the reserved marinade and a splash of water, then simmer covered 25 to 30 minutes.
Stir the onions back in, cook the rice, and portion into 14 containers.

name: High-Protein Cheeseburger Pasta
ingredients: 93/7 Ground Beef (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Penne Pasta (Barilla): 7 1/4 cups (14.5 oz each) (719 g)
Marinara Sauce (Great Value): about 3.5 cups (most of two 24 oz jars) (861 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
Yellow Onion: onion powder/fresh onion in most versions (250 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the penne to al dente per the box, then drain.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up. Drain any excess fat.
Pour the pasta sauce into the beef and simmer a couple of minutes until hot.
Add the drained penne and stir until every piece is coated.
Fold in the shredded mozzarella off the heat so it turns gooey.
head_steps: Boil the penne to al dente per the box and drain.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet and drain any excess fat.
Add the pasta sauce to the beef and simmer until hot.
Stir in the drained penne until coated.
Fold in the mozzarella off the heat.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 equal containers.

name: Cheesy Beef and Broccoli Rice Bowls
ingredients: 93/7 Ground Beef (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Rice (Member's Mark): 3.5 cups dry jasmine (700 g)
Broccoli Florets (Great Value): 7 cups (about 21 oz) (595 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up. Drain any excess.
Add the broccoli and the beef broth, cover, and steam a few minutes until the broccoli is bright and tender.
Combine the rice, beef, and broccoli in your big pot and stir. Fold in the shredded cheddar.
head_steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet and drain any excess.
Add the broccoli and beef broth, cover, and steam until tender.
Combine rice, beef, and broccoli and fold in the cheddar.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.

name: Cheesy Zucchini Beef and Rice Skillet
ingredients: Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 3/4 cups (196 g)
Vegetable Oil (Great Value): 2 tbsp canola oil (40 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (2 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Rinse the rice and cook it according to the package. Set it aside to steam while you build the skillet.
Heat a large skillet over medium high heat with a little of the canola oil. Add the lean ground beef and brown it, breaking it apart as it cooks until there is no more pink.
Stir in the diced yellow onion, green bell peppers, and minced garlic with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until they start to soften.
Add the diced zucchini, the taco seasoning, the beef broth, and the canned diced tomatoes with their juice. Stir it all together so the seasoning coats everything.
Let it simmer 5 to 7 minutes until the zucchini is tender and the broth cooks down to coat everything.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fat free cheddar until it melts into the mix. Serve over the cooked rice, or fold the rice right into the skillet.
head_steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Rinse the rice and cook it according to the package. Set it aside to steam while you build the skillet.
Heat a large skillet over medium high heat with a little of the canola oil. Add the lean ground beef and brown it, breaking it apart as it cooks until there is no more pink.
Stir in the diced yellow onion, green bell peppers, and minced garlic with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until they start to soften.
Add the diced zucchini, the taco seasoning, the beef broth, and the canned diced tomatoes with their juice. Stir it all together so the seasoning coats everything.
Let it simmer 5 to 7 minutes until the zucchini is tender and the broth cooks down to coat everything.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fat free cheddar until it melts into the mix. Serve over the cooked rice, or fold the rice right into the skillet.

name: Chicken Enchilada Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Rice (Member's Mark): 3.5 cups dry jasmine (700 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4 cans, drained (910 g)
Enchilada Sauce (Old El Paso): 1 3/4 cups (about 1 3/4 cups) (420 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 1/2 cups, drained (420 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Cube the chicken and cook in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside.
Pour in the enchilada sauce and stir to coat the chicken.
Drain the beans and corn and warm them through.
Combine the rice, saucy chicken, beans, and corn in your big pot and stir. Fold in the shredded cheddar.
head_steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Cube and cook the chicken until it reaches 165F.
Add the enchilada sauce and stir to coat.
Drain and warm the beans and corn.
Combine rice, chicken, beans, and corn and fold in the cheddar.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.

name: Chicken Pad Thai Noodle Bowls
ingredients: Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 30.75 oz dry (875 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 6.75 oz (189 g)
Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 2.25 lb (1050 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the rice noodles in hot tap water 20 to 30 minutes until pliable but not fully soft, then drain. They finish cooking in the pot.
Stir the sauce together: fish sauce, brown sugar, oyster sauce, and lime juice. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Slice the chicken thin, season with salt and pepper, and sear it in batches in a little of the oil over high heat until cooked through to 165 F. Set aside.
In the same pot, cook the sliced onion and garlic in more oil until fragrant. Push everything to one side, pour in the beaten eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add the drained noodles and the sauce. Toss and fry 2 to 3 minutes, until the noodles soak up the sauce and turn glossy. Return the chicken and toss once more.
Portion into 14 containers and top each with a spoonful of chopped peanuts so they keep their crunch.
head_steps: Soak rice noodles in hot water until pliable, then drain.
Mix fish sauce, brown sugar, oyster sauce, and lime juice into the pad thai sauce.
Sear sliced chicken to 165 F, then cook onion and garlic and scramble the eggs in the same pot.
Add noodles and sauce, toss until glossy, and return the chicken.
Portion into 14 containers and top with chopped peanuts.

name: Chicken Parmesan Pasta
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Penne Pasta (Barilla): 7 1/4 cups (14.5 oz each) (719 g)
Marinara Sauce (Great Value): about 3.5 cups (861 g)
Parmesan Cheese (Great Value): 7/8 cup grated (98 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (5 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the penne to al dente per the box, then drain.
Cube the chicken and cook in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside.
Pour in the pasta sauce and simmer a couple of minutes until hot.
Add the drained penne and stir to coat, then fold in the parmesan.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top and cover for a minute until it melts.
head_steps: Boil the penne to al dente and drain.
Cube and cook the chicken until it reaches 165F.
Add the pasta sauce and simmer until hot.
Stir in the penne and fold in the parmesan.
Top with mozzarella and cover until melted.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.

name: Claypot Chicken and Mushroom Rice
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1588 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 0.5 cups (126 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into bite sized pieces and marinate them with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sesame oil, and a little salt and pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Slice the mushrooms and the sausage thin. Thin matters, because everything on top needs to cook through in the same time the rice does.
Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then put it in a heavy pot or rice cooker with the chicken broth.
Lay the marinated chicken, mushrooms, and sausage across the top of the rice. Do not stir. The rice steams underneath while the toppings drip down into it, and stirring destroys the whole method.
Cook covered on low for about 25 minutes, or run a standard rice cooker cycle, then let it sit covered off the heat for 10 more minutes.
Lift the lid, pour any remaining marinade over the top, and now fold everything together gently.
Scatter the sliced green onions across the pot before portioning.
head_steps: Marinate the cut chicken thighs in oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sesame oil for 30 minutes.
Slice the mushrooms and sausage thin.
Rinse the rice and combine it with the chicken broth in a heavy pot or rice cooker.
Lay the chicken, mushrooms, and sausage on top without stirring and cook covered about 25 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes, fold everything together, top with green onions, and portion into 14 containers.

name: Cottage Pie
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel and cube the potatoes and boil them in salted water until a knife slides through with no resistance.
While they cook, brown the ground beef in the olive oil in a wide pot over medium high heat, breaking it up as it goes, until no pink remains.
Add the chopped onion, carrots, celery, and garlic and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, then pour in the beef broth and Worcestershire sauce with the thyme and bay leaves.
Simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the filling is thick enough to hold a line when you drag a spoon through it. Pull the bay leaves.
Drain and mash the potatoes with the milk and butter, season them well, and spread them over the filling in a large baking dish or two sheet pans.
Scatter the parmesan on top and bake at 400F for 25 to 30 minutes, until the top is browned and the edges bubble.
head_steps: Boil the peeled potatoes until tender.
Brown the ground beef, then soften onion, carrot, celery, and garlic with it.
Stir in flour and tomato paste, add broth, Worcestershire, thyme, and bay, and simmer until thick.
Mash the potatoes with milk and butter and spread them over the filling.
Top with parmesan, bake at 400F for 25 to 30 minutes, and cut into 14 squares.

name: Creamy Ground Turkey and Chorizo Pasta
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 49.5 oz dry (1400 g)
1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 14.75 oz (420 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the pasta shells 1 minute short of package time. Before draining, scoop out and save about 3 cups of the starchy pasta water.

Brown the chorizo in a splash of oil in your big pot, breaking it up, then add the ground turkey and cook until no pink remains, seasoning with the Italian seasoning, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Add the diced zucchini and cook 4 to 5 minutes until just tender.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes and cook 3 to 4 minutes until they blister and start to break down.
Drop the cream cheese in chunks and stir with a ladle of the reserved pasta water until it melts into a smooth sauce. Add more pasta water until it is silky.
Fold in the drained shells, lemon juice, parmesan, and basil, tossing until every shell is coated.
Portion into 14 containers while the sauce is still loose; it thickens as it cools.
head_steps: Boil the shells just short of done and reserve 3 cups pasta water.
Brown chorizo, then the seasoned ground turkey until no pink remains.
Cook zucchini until tender, then blister the cherry tomatoes.
Melt in cream cheese with pasta water to make a silky sauce.
Fold in shells, lemon juice, parmesan, and basil, then portion into 14 containers.

name: Curried Sausages with Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep skillet and brown the sausages whole on all sides. Take them out and set them aside once they have color.
Slice the onions, slice the carrots into coins and mince the garlic.
Cook the onions in the sausage drippings until soft, then add the garlic and the carrots.
Sprinkle the flour and the curry powder over the vegetables and stir for a full minute. Cooking the curry powder in the fat is what wakes it up, and skipping this leaves it tasting dusty.
Stream in the chicken broth while stirring so no lumps form, add the sugar, and bring the gravy to a simmer until it thickens.
Slice the browned sausages into thick coins, return them to the pan, and simmer so they soak up the gravy and finish cooking through.
Stir in the frozen peas at the very end, season with salt and black pepper, and serve it over hot rice.
head_steps: Brown the whole sausages in vegetable oil and set them aside.
Cook the sliced onions in the drippings, then add the garlic and sliced carrots.
Stir the flour and curry powder into the vegetables and cook for a minute.
Stream in the chicken broth with the sugar and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Slice the sausages, return them to the gravy, stir in the peas, and serve over rice.

name: Fajita Chicken Rice Bowl
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 5.5 lb raw (2495 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 5 1/4 cups (910 g)
Rice (Member's Mark): 4 cups dry jasmine (800 g)
Fajita Seasoning (Taco Bell): 6 packets (Taco Bell) (238 g)
Yellow Onion: 1 small onion, sliced (300 g)
steps: Weigh your empty pot first. Put the largest pot you'll use to mix everything onto your large scale and write down its weight. You'll need that number at the end to portion accurately.
Cook the rice (4 cups dry jasmine plus water per the package) and set aside.
Slice the bell peppers into strips.
Cube and cook the chicken breast in a large skillet until done.
Add the fajita seasoning with a splash of water, toss in the peppers, and simmer until the peppers soften and everything is coated.
Warm the black beans through.
Combine the rice, seasoned chicken and peppers, and beans back in the big pot and stir.
head_steps: Cook 4 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Slice the bell peppers into strips.
Cube and cook the chicken breast in a large skillet until done.
Add the fajita seasoning with a splash of water, toss in the peppers, and simmer until the peppers soften and everything is coated.
Warm the black beans through.
Combine the rice, seasoned chicken and peppers, and beans and stir.

name: Filipino Beef Pares Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into large cubes. Sear them hard in a little oil, in batches, until they have real color on at least two sides.
Add chopped onion, half the garlic, and the ginger to the pot and cook until the onion goes soft and translucent.
Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, and brown sugar. Add the bay leaves, black pepper, and salt, scraping the browned bits off the bottom.
Cover and simmer low for 2 to 2.5 hours, until the beef pulls apart with a spoon. Add water if the pot gets too dry.
Uncover for the last 20 minutes and let the sauce reduce until it coats the beef instead of pooling around it.
For the garlic rice, fry the remaining sliced garlic in the rest of the oil until golden, then toss in the cooked cold rice and stir until every grain is coated and hot.
Finish with sliced green onions over the beef.
head_steps: Sear cubed chuck roast in batches until well browned.
Cook onion, garlic, and ginger in the same pot until soft.
Add broth, soy sauce, brown sugar, bay leaves, black pepper, and salt and simmer covered 2 to 2.5 hours.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until it coats the beef.
Fry sliced garlic in oil, toss with cold cooked rice, and portion into 14 containers.

name: Ghanaian Shoko (Beef and Spinach Stew)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck into bite sized cubes, season with salt and pepper, and brown them hard in oil in batches. Set the beef aside.
Blend the diced tomatoes, a large share of the onion, the bell peppers, jalapeno, garlic, and ginger into a rough puree.
Cook the remaining chopped onion in the same pot until soft, then pour in the puree and fry it, stirring often, until it darkens and the raw tomato smell is gone.
Grind the peanuts to a coarse meal and stir them in along with the coriander, cumin, and other pantry spices.
Return the beef with the beef broth, cover, and simmer 60 to 90 minutes until the beef is fork tender and the sauce has tightened.
Stir in the chopped spinach and cook 5 more minutes, just until it is fully wilted and folded through.
Cook the rice separately, then taste the stew and correct the salt.
head_steps: Brown cubed chuck roast in batches and set it aside.
Blend tomatoes, onion, bell pepper, jalapeno, garlic, and ginger into a puree.
Fry the puree in the pot until it darkens, then stir in ground peanuts and spices.
Return the beef with broth and simmer 60 to 90 minutes until tender.
Fold in the spinach, cook the rice, and portion into 14 containers.

name: Hot Honey Chicken and Broccoli Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Rice (Member's Mark): 3.5 cups dry jasmine (700 g)
Broccoli Florets (Great Value): 7 cups (about 21 oz) (595 g)
Hot Honey (Better Goods): about 7 tbsp (7/16 cup) (147 g)
Olive Oil: ~2 tbsp (cook chicken/roast broccoli) (100 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Cube the chicken and cook in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside.
Steam or microwave the broccoli until bright and tender.
Turn the heat to low, drizzle the hot honey over the chicken, and toss until glazed.
Combine the rice, hot honey chicken, and broccoli in your big pot and stir.
head_steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Cube and cook the chicken breast until it reaches 165F.
Steam or microwave the broccoli until tender.
Lower the heat, drizzle hot honey over the chicken, and toss to glaze.
Combine rice, chicken, and broccoli and stir.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.

name: Italian Sausage Penne with Peppers
ingredients: Hot Italian Sausage (Johnsonville): 2 lb (two ~1 lb packages) (735 g)
Penne Pasta (Barilla): 7 1/4 cups (14.5 oz each) (719 g)
Marinara Sauce (Great Value): 4 1/3 cups (24 oz each) (1076 g)
Parmesan Cheese (Great Value): 1 cup grated (98 g)
Yellow Onion: 1/2 yellow onion, sliced (220 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the penne to al dente per the box, then drain.
Slice the sausage into coins (or squeeze it from the casing) and brown it in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the sliced peppers and cook until they soften, a few minutes.
Pour in the pasta sauce and simmer until hot.
Add the drained penne, stir to coat, then fold in the parmesan off the heat.
head_steps: Boil the penne to al dente and drain.
Brown the sliced sausage in a large skillet.
Add the peppers and cook until softened.
Add the pasta sauce and simmer until hot.
Stir in the penne and fold in the parmesan off the heat.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.

name: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice with Sausage
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins and brown them in the vegetable oil in a large pot, then set them aside.
Add the diced onion, celery, and green bell pepper to the same pot and cook until softened and the bottom of the pot picks up color.
Stir in the garlic and the dried seasonings and cook for a minute so the spices bloom in the fat.
Add the kidney beans with their liquid and the chicken broth, then return the sausage to the pot.
Simmer uncovered for at least forty minutes, mashing some of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy.
Cook the rice separately according to the package while the beans simmer.
Fish out the bay leaves, season with salt and black pepper to taste, and serve the beans over the rice.
head_steps: Slice and brown the smoked sausage, then set it aside.
Cook the onion, celery, and bell pepper in the same pot until soft.
Add garlic and dried seasonings and bloom them in the fat.
Add the beans, broth, and sausage and simmer at least forty minutes, mashing some beans to thicken.
Cook the rice separately.
Season, remove the bay leaves, and portion beans over rice into 14 containers.

name: Musakhan (Sumac Chicken and Caramelized Onions)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.75 lb (1750 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice all the onions thin. This is the longest part of the recipe and there is no way around it, so put on something to listen to and get it done.

Toss the chicken thighs with some of the olive oil, salt, black pepper, ground allspice, ground cinnamon, ground cumin, garam masala, ground nutmeg and a generous spoonful of the sumac. Let them sit while the oven heats to 425F.

Cook the sliced onions in the rest of the olive oil in your largest pot over medium-low heat for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they collapse into a soft sweet jam. Low and slow. If they are browning fast, the heat is too high.
Stir the bulk of the sumac into the cooked onions and let it cook another 5 minutes until they turn deep red and smell tart.
Roast the seasoned chicken on a sheet pan for 25 to 30 minutes, until it reads 165F and the edges are dark. Save every drop of the pan drippings.
Warm the flatbreads, tear them into large pieces, and toss them in your mixing pot with the pan drippings so they soak up the fat rather than staying dry.
Chop the chicken, fold it together with the sumac onions and the soaked bread, and finish with the chopped cilantro.
head_steps: Season the chicken thighs with olive oil, sumac, allspice, cinnamon, cumin, garam masala and nutmeg.
Cook the thinly sliced onions in olive oil over medium-low heat for 30 to 40 minutes until jammy.
Stir the remaining sumac into the onions and cook 5 more minutes.
Roast the chicken at 425F for 25 to 30 minutes until it reads 165F, saving the drippings.
Toss torn warm flatbread in the drippings, fold with the onions and chopped chicken, and portion into 14 containers.

name: Slow Cooker Butter Chicken Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3000 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Add the chicken breast, chopped onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger to the crock.
Pour in both cans of tomato sauce, drop in the butter with a drizzle of olive oil and the lemon juice, then stir in the garam masala, chili powder, ground cumin, cayenne, and a bay leaf.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken is tender.
Shred the chicken, fish out the bay leaf, then stir in the milk, Greek yogurt, and half and half for that creamy finish, and season with salt and pepper.
Cook the rice while the sauce warms through.
Spoon the butter chicken over rice and serve.

Cook the rice while the sauce warms through.
Spoon the butter chicken over rice and serve.

name: Slow Cooker Chicken Tortilla Soup Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3000 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 2 cans (500 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 1/2 cups (400 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 1 cup (112 g)
Enchilada Sauce (Old El Paso): 10 oz can (570 g)
Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 4.5 oz can (255 g)
Lime Juice: juice of 1 lime (60 g)
steps: Add the chicken breast, crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, enchilada sauce, and diced green chiles to the crock. Stir in the chopped onion, garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt, pepper, and the bay leaf.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken is tender.
Fish out the bay leaf, shred the chicken, then stir in the black beans and corn.
Let it heat through for another 15 to 20 minutes, then stir in the lime juice.
Cook your rice while the pot finishes.
Spoon over rice and finish each bowl with a little cheddar.

name: Slow Cooker Cuban Mojo Pork Bowls
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 7 cups (1200 g)
steps: Place the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker.
Whisk the orange juice, lime juice, garlic, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper together, then pour it over the pork.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until fork-tender.
Shred the pork, then whisk the cornstarch with a splash of the cooking liquid and stir it in with the chopped cilantro and mint to thicken the mojo sauce.
Warm the seasoned black beans and spoon them into your bowls as the base.
Top the beans with the mojo pork and divide into containers.

name: Slow Cooker Dr Pepper Pulled Pork Bowls
ingredients: BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) (Sweet Baby Ray's): 1 bottle (360 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): for rub (3 g)
steps: Set the pork loin in the slow cooker and scatter the sliced onion around it.
Pour the zero-sugar soda over the pork until it is about halfway up the sides.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork shreds easily.
Drain off most of the liquid, then shred the pork right in the pot.
Stir in the BBQ sauce and let it warm through for a few minutes.
Serve over cooked potatoes and divide into containers.

name: Slow Cooker Mediterranean Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3450 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Add the chicken, sliced onion, chicken broth, olive oil, garlic, lime juice, oregano, thyme, rosemary, bay leaf, salt, and pepper to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken is tender all the way through.
Stir in the chopped roasted red peppers and olives during the last 30 minutes.
Shred the chicken into the pot so it soaks up the savory, briny juices.
Discard the bay leaf and serve over white rice with plenty of the peppers and olives spooned on top.

name: Thai Turkey Larb Bowls
ingredients: Jalapeno: 3-4 dry chiles or 1.5 Tbsp chile powder (35 g)
Fresh Cilantro: 1/2 cup rough chopped (30 g)
steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey, breaking it into fine crumbles.
Add the chopped onion and green peppers and cook until they soften.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, and honey and let it bubble a minute so the turkey soaks up that salty sweet-and-sour balance. The fish sauce is the backbone of larb, not an optional splash.
Stir in the ground dried chiles for heat, then pull the pan off the stove.
Fold in the chopped fresh cilantro and fresh mint so they stay bright. Those herbs are half of what makes this larb, not a garnish set on the side.
Serve it over cooked white rice with extra lime on the side.
head_steps: Brown the ground turkey in a little olive oil, then soften the chopped onion and green peppers.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, and honey and let it soak into the turkey.
Stir in the ground dried chiles off the heat, then fold in the fresh cilantro and mint.
Serve over cooked white rice with extra lime on the side.

name: Turkey Bolognese Penne
ingredients: Penne Pasta (Barilla): 7 1/4 cups (14.5 oz each) (719 g)
Marinara Sauce (Great Value): 4 1/3 cups (24 oz each) (1076 g)
Parmesan Cheese (Great Value): about 7/8 cup grated (98 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the penne to al dente per the box, then drain.
Brown the ground turkey in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks.
Pour in the pasta sauce and simmer 10 minutes to let it thicken into a bolognese.
Add the drained penne and stir to coat, then fold in the parmesan off the heat.
head_steps: Boil the penne to al dente and drain.
Brown the ground turkey in a large pot.
Add the pasta sauce and simmer 10 minutes to thicken.
Stir in the penne and fold in the parmesan off the heat.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.

name: Turkey Meatball Sub Bake
ingredients: Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 16.75 oz (476 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Chop the smoked turkey sausage fine, or run it through a food processor, and mix it with the ground turkey, the eggs, the bread crumbs, the parmesan, minced garlic, minced onion, chopped mushrooms, salt, and black pepper.
Roll the mixture into meatballs and set them on lined sheet pans. Two per serving is the target size, so aim a little bigger than a golf ball.
Bake at 400F for 20 minutes until browned and cooked through to 165F.
Warm the marinara in a pot, then slide the baked meatballs in and simmer them 15 minutes so they drink up the sauce instead of just wearing it.
Portion the meatballs and sauce into the containers using the weighed-pot method, dividing them evenly across all fourteen.
Split the buns and lay them out. Do not assemble them all now, since bread that sits in sauce for four days is a texture nobody wants.
Shred or portion out the mozzarella and keep it in its own small container.
head_steps: Finely chop the smoked turkey sausage and mix it with ground turkey, eggs, bread crumbs, parmesan, garlic, onion, mushrooms, salt, and pepper.
Roll into meatballs and bake at 400F for 20 minutes to 165F.
Simmer the meatballs in warmed marinara for 15 minutes.
Portion the meatballs and sauce evenly into the 14 containers.
Pack the split buns and mozzarella separately to assemble and broil fresh.

name: Turkey Taco Rice Skillet
ingredients: Rice (Member's Mark): 3.5 cups dry jasmine (700 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4 cans, drained (910 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 5 cups, drained (840 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (~7 oz) (196 g)
Salsa (Pace): 1 cup chunky tomato salsa (per 4) (850 g)
Chicken Broth (Swanson): 3 cups (to cook rice in-pan) (2000 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the taco seasoning and a splash of water and stir until coated.
Drain and rinse the beans and corn, then warm them through.
Combine the rice, turkey, beans, and corn in your big pot and stir. Fold in the shredded cheddar.
head_steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet, breaking it up.
Stir in the taco seasoning with a splash of water.
Drain and warm the beans and corn.
Combine rice, turkey, beans, and corn and fold in the cheddar.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 containers.

name: Turkish Iskender Turkey Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (2 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the flatbread into bite-sized squares, spread them on a sheet pan, and toast at 375F for 8 to 10 minutes until dry and lightly golden. They need to be dry enough to hold up under sauce.
Char the green peppers whole under the broiler for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until the skins blister, then slice them into strips.

Heat most of the olive oil in a large skillet and cook the sliced onion for 6 minutes, then add the tomato paste, paprika, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper and cook two minutes until the paste darkens.
Add the canned diced tomatoes and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the sauce reduces and thickens enough to hold its shape on a spoon.
Sear the sliced turkey breast in the remaining olive oil over high heat in batches, just long enough to get color on the edges without drying it out.
Whisk the Greek yogurt smooth with a pinch of salt and a splash of water so it pours rather than sits in a lump.

Build the bowls: toasted bread cubes on the bottom, seared turkey over them, tomato sauce spooned across, melted butter drizzled over the top, charred peppers on the side, and the yogurt in its own corner.
head_steps: Cut the flatbread into squares and toast at 375F for 8 to 10 minutes until dry.
Char the green peppers under the broiler until blistered, then slice into strips.
Cook the onion in olive oil, add the tomato paste, paprika, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper, then the diced tomatoes, and simmer 20 to 25 minutes.
Sear the sliced turkey breast in batches over high heat, and whisk the Greek yogurt smooth with salt.
Layer bread, turkey, tomato sauce, and melted butter, add peppers and yogurt on the side, and portion into 14 containers.
